On this page

Warfarin PK/PD ​

Thirty-two subjects took one oral dose of warfarin, 1.5 mg per kg of body weight. Their plasma warfarin concentration was measured for up to 120 hours, and their prothrombin complex activity, the anticoagulant effect in percent of normal, for up to 144 hours. The data are O'Reilly's warfarin data as Sebastian Weber distributed them with his StanCon 2018 example (the file and its licence).

This page fits that example's models in BRM, on all 32 subjects, and shows what they estimate:

  • Weber's two-stage workflow: a population PK model, then a turnover PD model that takes each subject's PK posterior medians as fixed inputs;

  • a joint model: one posterior, in which the PD data also inform the PK quantities.

Every declaration below is read from the checked-in scripts when the docs are built, and every number and figure comes from research/warfarin/fit.jl and research/warfarin/figures.jl.

The data ​

warfarin_data() reads the file into one entry per subject (dose, weight) and one vector per subject and channel (sampling times, observations): 32 subjects, 253 concentration measurements and 232 activity measurements. Five concentrations measured half an hour after the dose, all zero, are left out, as in Weber's data preparation: the model lets the lag before absorption be as long as one hour, so a measurement inside the lag carries no information about the parameters.

Stage 1: population PK ​

A one-compartment model with first-order absorption and a lag before absorption starts. Each subject has four parameters: the lag time tlag, a logistic fraction of one hour; the absorption rate ka; the clearance CL and the volume V, which scale with body weight relative to 70 kg with the allometric exponents 0.75 and 1. Each is a population value plus an independent subject effect on the log (for the lag, the logit) scale, written as a linear predictor with a random intercept; the weight scaling is a formula offset. The plate computes the closed-form concentration course of one subject, and observes it with Weber's gamma2_overdisp family, a gamma distribution with mean mu and variance sigma² + mu² / kappa; kappa is scaled by 25.

Population PK
panes: brm|stanblocks|rkppl|stan|jax:1
julia
function warfarin_pk_brmi(data = warfarin_data())
    return @brm data begin
        sigma_pk ~ Normal(0.0, 2.0; lower=0.0)
        kappa_pk ~ Gamma(0.2, 5.0)

        lag_logit ~ 1 + (1 | tlag_bsv | subject)
        log_ka ~ 1 + (1 | ka_bsv | subject)
        # Allometric weight scaling as a formula OFFSET (fixed exponents 0.75 / 1.0),
        # not hand-wired in the kernel cell: clearance ~ weight^0.75, volume ~ weight^1.
        log_cl0 ~ 1 + offset(0.75 * log_weight_ratio) + (1 | cl_bsv | subject)
        log_v0 ~ 1 + offset(log_weight_ratio) + (1 | v_bsv | subject)

        effect(lag_logit, :) ~ Normal(0.0, 2.0)
        effect(log_ka, :) ~ Normal(log(1.0), log(2.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_cl0, :) ~ Normal(log(0.1), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_v0, :) ~ Normal(log(10.0), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        sd(:, tlag_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, ka_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, cl_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, v_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)

        # One cell per subject: its sampling times, dose and observed
        # concentrations, and its own values of the four linear predictors.
        # log_cl0 / log_v0 already carry the allometric offset (formula term above).
        @plate for i in eachindex(lag_logit)
            log_tlag = -log1pexp(-lag_logit[i])    # log(tlag), tlag = logistic(lag_logit) < tlagMax = 1
            pk_pred[i] = exp.(warfarin_pk_logconcentration(
                pk_time[i], log(dose[i]), log_ka[i], log_cl0[i], log_v0[i], log_tlag,
            )) .+ 1e-5
            pk_dv[i] ~ warfarin_gamma2_overdisp(pk_pred[i], sigma_pk, kappa_pk * 25.0)
        end
    end
end

stan
functions {
matrix hcat(vector x) {
    int n = dims(x)[1];
    return to_matrix(x, n, 1);
}
int ragged_end(array[] int ends, int i) {
    return ends[i];
}
int ragged_start(
    array[] int ends,
    int i
) {
    if((i == 1)) {
        return 1;
    } else {
        return (1 + ends[(i - 1)]);
    }
}
vector jbroadcasted_exp(
    vector x1
) {
    int n = dims(x1)[1];
    vector[n] rv;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        rv[i] = exp(broadcasted_getindex(x1, i));
    }
    return rv;
}
real broadcasted_getindex(vector x, int i) {
    return x[i];
}
vector warfarin_pk_logconcentration(
    vector tad,
    real log_dose,
    real log_ka,
    real log_cl,
    real log_v,
    real log_tlag
) {
    int n = dims(tad)[1];
    real log_ke = (log_cl - log_v);
    real log_delta = warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(log_ka, log_ke);
    real log_scale = (((log_dose - log_v) + log_ka) - log_delta);
    vector[n] value;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        if((tad[i] <= exp(log_tlag))) {
            value[i] = negative_infinity();
        } else {
            real log_tad = log((tad[i] - exp(log_tlag)));
            real a = (-exp((log_ke + log_tad)));
            real b = (-exp((log_ka + log_tad)));
            value[i] = (log_scale + warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(a, b));
        }
    }
    return value;
}
real warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(
    real log_a,
    real log_b
) {
    return (0.5 * log_diff_exp(log_sum_exp((2.0 * log_a), (2.0 * log_b)), (log(2.0) + log_a + log_b)));
}
real warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdf(
    vector y,
    vector mu,
    real sigma,
    real kappa
) {
    int n = dims(y)[1];
    if (dims(mu)[1] != n) reject("warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdf: dim mismatch — `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `y` dim 1. `n` sizes: `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], "), `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ").");
    real lp = 0.0;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        real variance = (square(sigma) + (square(mu[i]) / kappa));
        real shape = (square(mu[i]) / variance);
        real rate = (mu[i] / variance);
        lp += gamma_lpdf(y[i] | shape, rate);
    }
    return lp;
}
vector warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdfs(
    vector y,
    vector mu,
    real sigma,
    real kappa
) {
    int n = dims(y)[1];
    if (dims(mu)[1] != n) reject("warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdfs: dim mismatch — `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `y` dim 1. `n` sizes: `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], "), `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ").");
    vector[n] lp;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        real variance = (square(sigma) + (square(mu[i]) / kappa));
        real shape = (square(mu[i]) / variance);
        real rate = (mu[i] / variance);
        lp[i] = gamma_lpdf(y[i] | shape, rate);
    }
    return lp;
}
vector warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_vector_rng(
    int anontok__1,
    vector mu,
    real sigma,
    real kappa
) {
    int n = anontok__1;
    if (dims(mu)[1] != n) reject("warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_rng: dim mismatch — `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `anontok__1` dim 1. `n` sizes: `anontok__1` dim 1 (= ", anontok__1, "), `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ").");
    vector[n] draw;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        draw[i] = warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_rng(mu[i], sigma, kappa);
    }
    return draw;
}
real warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_rng(
    real mu,
    real sigma,
    real kappa
) {
    real variance = (square(sigma) + (square(mu) / kappa));
    real shape = (square(mu) / variance);
    real rate = (mu / variance);
    return gamma_rng(shape, rate);
}
}

RK source: `pk_dv ~ warfarin_gamma2_overdisp(...)` needs a scalar `_rk_observation_source!` provider on the RK backend; this Stan-only family has no scalar Julia constructor

The population priors, the half-normal priors on the four subject SDs, the maximal lag of one hour and the overdispersion scaling are Weber's. One spelling differs from his Stan program: log_inv_logit(x) is written -log1pexp(-x), the same function.

Each panel is one subject: the observed concentrations, and the median with the 50 % and 95 % bands of the posterior predictive distribution at the sampling times. The bands include the observation noise, so a well-fitted subject has about half its points inside the inner band. The figures on this page are drawn when the docs are built, from the committed tables.

The handoff ​

The PD stage takes, for each subject, the posterior medians of log(tlag), log(ka), log(CL) and log(V) from the PK fit, with the weight effect inside log(CL) and log(V). They enter the PD model as the data columns pk_log_tlag, pk_log_ka, pk_log_cl and pk_log_v (research/warfarin/results/pk_subject_medians.tsv), not as parameters, so the PD data cannot update them and the PK uncertainty does not reach the PD predictions.

Stage 2: turnover PD ​

Prothrombin complex activity R is produced at a constant rate kin and removed at the rate kout R; warfarin inhibits the production: dR/dt = kin (1 - C / (C + EC50)) - kout R, with R(0) = R0 = kin / kout, the steady state before the dose. Each subject has R0, the turnover time 1/kout and EC50, each a population value with an independent subject effect on the log scale. The plate solves the ODE for one subject with Stan's ode_rk45_tol at that subject's fixed PK medians, and observes the activity with the same gamma family, kappa scaled by 625.

brm-comparison
Turnover PD on fixed PK medians
panes: brm|stanblocks|rkppl|stan|jax:1
julia
function warfarin_pd_brmi(data = warfarin_pd_data())
    return @brm data begin
        sigma_pd ~ Normal(0.0, 10.0; lower=0.0)
        kappa_pd ~ Gamma(0.2, 5.0)

        log_r0 ~ 1 + (1 | r0_bsv | subject)
        log_inv_kout ~ 1 + (1 | kout_bsv | subject)
        log_ec50 ~ 1 + (1 | ec50_bsv | subject)

        effect(log_r0, :) ~ Normal(log(80.0), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_inv_kout, :) ~ Normal(log(30.0), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_ec50, :) ~ Normal(log(2.5), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        sd(:, r0_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, kout_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, ec50_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)

        # One cell per subject. pk_log_* are that subject's fixed PK posterior
        # medians from the first stage: data columns, one value per subject.
        @plate for i in eachindex(log_r0)
            pd_pred[i] = warfarin_turnover_prediction(
                pd_time[i], log(dose[i]), pk_log_ka[i], pk_log_cl[i], pk_log_v[i],
                pk_log_tlag[i], log_r0[i], log_inv_kout[i], log_ec50[i],
            )
            pd_dv[i] ~ warfarin_gamma2_overdisp(pd_pred[i], sigma_pd, kappa_pd * 625.0)
        end
    end
end

vector warfarin_turnover_prediction(
    vector times,
    real log_dose,
    real log_ka,
    real log_cl,
    real log_v,
    real log_tlag,
    real log_r0,
    real log_inv_kout,
    real log_ec50
) {
    int n = dims(times)[1];
    vector[1] initial_state = rep_vector(exp(log_r0), 1);
    array[dims(times)[1]] vector[1] trajectory = ode_rk45_tol(
        warfarin_turnover_rhs,
        initial_state,
        -0.0001,
        to_array_1d(times),
        1.0e-5,
        0.001,
        500,
        log_dose,
        log_ka,
        log_cl,
        log_v,
        log_tlag,
        log_r0,
        log_inv_kout,
        log_ec50
    );
    return to_vector(trajectory[:, 1]);
}
vector warfarin_turnover_rhs(
    real time,
    vector state,
    real log_dose,
    real log_ka,
    real log_cl,
    real log_v,
    real log_tlag,
    real log_r0,
    real log_inv_kout,
    real log_ec50
) {
    int m = dims(state)[1];
    real log_conc = warfarin_pk_logconcentration_one(time, log_dose, log_ka, log_cl, log_v, log_tlag);
    real log_kout = (-log_inv_kout);
    real log_kin = (log_r0 + log_kout);
    real log_inhibition = log_inv_logit((log_conc - log_ec50));
    vector[m] derivative;
    derivative[1] = (exp((log_kin + log1m_exp(log_inhibition))) - (state[1] * exp(log_kout)));
    return derivative;
}
real warfarin_pk_logconcentration_one(
    real time,
    real log_dose,
    real log_ka,
    real log_cl,
    real log_v,
    real log_tlag
) {
    if((time < exp(log_tlag))) {
        return -25.0;
    }
    real log_ke = (log_cl - log_v);
    real log_delta = warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(log_ka, log_ke);
    real log_scale = (((log_dose - log_v) + log_ka) - log_delta);
    real log_tad = log((time - exp(log_tlag)));
    real a = (-exp((log_ke + log_tad)));
    real b = (-exp((log_ka + log_tad)));
    return (log_scale + warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(a, b));
}

The joint model ​

The joint model declares the four PK and the three PD subject quantities once. Both plates read the same latent PK values: the PK plate predicts the concentrations, the PD plate solves the turnover ODE driven by them. So the PD data update the PK quantities too, and the PK uncertainty reaches the PD predictions. The observation families are unchanged, and the two channels keep independent residuals: they are measured at different times, in different units.

Joint PK/PD

julia
function warfarin_joint_brmi(data = warfarin_data())
    return @brm data begin
        sigma_pk ~ Normal(0.0, 2.0; lower=0.0)
        kappa_pk ~ Gamma(0.2, 5.0)
        sigma_pd ~ Normal(0.0, 10.0; lower=0.0)
        kappa_pd ~ Gamma(0.2, 5.0)

        lag_logit ~ 1 + (1 | tlag_bsv | subject)
        log_ka ~ 1 + (1 | ka_bsv | subject)
        # Allometric weight scaling as a formula OFFSET (fixed exponents 0.75 / 1.0),
        # shared by both the PK and PD cells below — not hand-wired in either cell.
        log_cl0 ~ 1 + offset(0.75 * log_weight_ratio) + (1 | cl_bsv | subject)
        log_v0 ~ 1 + offset(log_weight_ratio) + (1 | v_bsv | subject)
        log_r0 ~ 1 + (1 | r0_bsv | subject)
        log_inv_kout ~ 1 + (1 | kout_bsv | subject)
        log_ec50 ~ 1 + (1 | ec50_bsv | subject)

        effect(lag_logit, :) ~ Normal(0.0, 2.0)
        effect(log_ka, :) ~ Normal(log(1.0), log(2.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_cl0, :) ~ Normal(log(0.1), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_v0, :) ~ Normal(log(10.0), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_r0, :) ~ Normal(log(80.0), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_inv_kout, :) ~ Normal(log(30.0), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        effect(log_ec50, :) ~ Normal(log(2.5), log(10.0) / 1.96)
        sd(:, tlag_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, ka_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, cl_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, v_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, r0_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, kout_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)
        sd(:, ec50_bsv) ~ Normal(0.0, 0.5)

        # The PK cell: one subject's concentration course from its own latent
        # lag, absorption, clearance and volume.
        @plate for i in eachindex(lag_logit)
            log_tlag = -log1pexp(-lag_logit[i])    # log(tlag), tlag = logistic(lag_logit) < tlagMax = 1
            pk_pred[i] = exp.(warfarin_pk_logconcentration(
                pk_time[i], log(dose[i]), log_ka[i], log_cl0[i], log_v0[i], log_tlag,
            )) .+ 1e-5
            pk_pointwise_loglik = warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdfs(
                pk_dv[i], pk_pred[i], sigma_pk, kappa_pk * 25.0,
            )
            pk_dv[i] ~ warfarin_gamma2_overdisp(pk_pred[i], sigma_pk, kappa_pk * 25.0)
        end

        # The PD cell reads the same latent PK quantities, so the PD data update
        # them too; no fixed medians are handed over.
        @plate for i in eachindex(lag_logit)
            log_tlag = -log1pexp(-lag_logit[i])
            pd_pred[i] = warfarin_turnover_prediction(
                pd_time[i], log(dose[i]), log_ka[i], log_cl0[i], log_v0[i],
                log_tlag, log_r0[i], log_inv_kout[i], log_ec50[i],
            )
            pd_pointwise_loglik = warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdfs(
                pd_dv[i], pd_pred[i], sigma_pd, kappa_pd * 625.0,
            )
            pd_dv[i] ~ warfarin_gamma2_overdisp(pd_pred[i], sigma_pd, kappa_pd * 625.0)
        end
    end
end

stan
functions {
matrix hcat(vector x) {
    int n = dims(x)[1];
    return to_matrix(x, n, 1);
}
int ragged_end(array[] int ends, int i) {
    return ends[i];
}
int ragged_start(
    array[] int ends,
    int i
) {
    if((i == 1)) {
        return 1;
    } else {
        return (1 + ends[(i - 1)]);
    }
}
vector jbroadcasted_exp(
    vector x1
) {
    int n = dims(x1)[1];
    vector[n] rv;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        rv[i] = exp(broadcasted_getindex(x1, i));
    }
    return rv;
}
real broadcasted_getindex(vector x, int i) {
    return x[i];
}
vector warfarin_pk_logconcentration(
    vector tad,
    real log_dose,
    real log_ka,
    real log_cl,
    real log_v,
    real log_tlag
) {
    int n = dims(tad)[1];
    real log_ke = (log_cl - log_v);
    real log_delta = warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(log_ka, log_ke);
    real log_scale = (((log_dose - log_v) + log_ka) - log_delta);
    vector[n] value;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        if((tad[i] <= exp(log_tlag))) {
            value[i] = negative_infinity();
        } else {
            real log_tad = log((tad[i] - exp(log_tlag)));
            real a = (-exp((log_ke + log_tad)));
            real b = (-exp((log_ka + log_tad)));
            value[i] = (log_scale + warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(a, b));
        }
    }
    return value;
}
real warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(
    real log_a,
    real log_b
) {
    return (0.5 * log_diff_exp(log_sum_exp((2.0 * log_a), (2.0 * log_b)), (log(2.0) + log_a + log_b)));
}
vector warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdfs(
    vector y,
    vector mu,
    real sigma,
    real kappa
) {
    int n = dims(y)[1];
    if (dims(mu)[1] != n) reject("warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdfs: dim mismatch — `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `y` dim 1. `n` sizes: `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], "), `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ").");
    vector[n] lp;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        real variance = (square(sigma) + (square(mu[i]) / kappa));
        real shape = (square(mu[i]) / variance);
        real rate = (mu[i] / variance);
        lp[i] = gamma_lpdf(y[i] | shape, rate);
    }
    return lp;
}
vector warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_vector_rng(
    int anontok__1,
    vector mu,
    real sigma,
    real kappa
) {
    int n = anontok__1;
    if (dims(mu)[1] != n) reject("warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_rng: dim mismatch — `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `anontok__1` dim 1. `n` sizes: `anontok__1` dim 1 (= ", anontok__1, "), `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ").");
    vector[n] draw;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        draw[i] = warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_rng(mu[i], sigma, kappa);
    }
    return draw;
}
real warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_rng(
    real mu,
    real sigma,
    real kappa
) {
    real variance = (square(sigma) + (square(mu) / kappa));
    real shape = (square(mu) / variance);
    real rate = (mu / variance);
    return gamma_rng(shape, rate);
}
real warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdf(
    vector y,
    vector mu,
    real sigma,
    real kappa
) {
    int n = dims(y)[1];
    if (dims(mu)[1] != n) reject("warfarin_gamma2_overdisp_lpdf: dim mismatch — `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ") does not match `n` (= ", n, "), inferred from `y` dim 1. `n` sizes: `y` dim 1 (= ", dims(y)[1], "), `mu` dim 1 (= ", dims(mu)[1], ").");
    real lp = 0.0;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        real variance = (square(sigma) + (square(mu[i]) / kappa));
        real shape = (square(mu[i]) / variance);
        real rate = (mu[i] / variance);
        lp += gamma_lpdf(y[i] | shape, rate);
    }
    return lp;
}
vector warfarin_turnover_prediction(
    vector times,
    real log_dose,
    real log_ka,
    real log_cl,
    real log_v,
    real log_tlag,
    real log_r0,
    real log_inv_kout,
    real log_ec50
) {
    int n = dims(times)[1];
    vector[1] initial_state = rep_vector(exp(log_r0), 1);
    array[dims(times)[1]] vector[1] trajectory = ode_rk45_tol(
        warfarin_turnover_rhs,
        initial_state,
        -0.0001,
        to_array_1d(times),
        1.0e-5,
        0.001,
        500,
        log_dose,
        log_ka,
        log_cl,
        log_v,
        log_tlag,
        log_r0,
        log_inv_kout,
        log_ec50
    );
    return to_vector(trajectory[:, 1]);
}
vector warfarin_turnover_rhs(
    real time,
    vector state,
    real log_dose,
    real log_ka,
    real log_cl,
    real log_v,
    real log_tlag,
    real log_r0,
    real log_inv_kout,
    real log_ec50
) {
    int m = dims(state)[1];
    real log_conc = warfarin_pk_logconcentration_one(time, log_dose, log_ka, log_cl, log_v, log_tlag);
    real log_kout = (-log_inv_kout);
    real log_kin = (log_r0 + log_kout);
    real log_inhibition = log_inv_logit((log_conc - log_ec50));
    vector[m] derivative;
    derivative[1] = (exp((log_kin + log1m_exp(log_inhibition))) - (state[1] * exp(log_kout)));
    return derivative;
}
real warfarin_pk_logconcentration_one(
    real time,
    real log_dose,
    real log_ka,
    real log_cl,
    real log_v,
    real log_tlag
) {
    if((time < exp(log_tlag))) {
        return -25.0;
    }
    real log_ke = (log_cl - log_v);
    real log_delta = warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(log_ka, log_ke);
    real log_scale = (((log_dose - log_v) + log_ka) - log_delta);
    real log_tad = log((time - exp(log_tlag)));
    real a = (-exp((log_ke + log_tad)));
    real b = (-exp((log_ka + log_tad)));
    return (log_scale + warfarin_log_diff_exp_abs(a, b));
}
}

the two-stage fits (blue) and the joint model (orange): median and 95 % interval, one panel per quantity on its own scale."}

Each panel is one population quantity; the blue interval is the two-stage estimate, the orange one the joint model's. The two agree on this data. The PK quantities move by less than their interval widths: clearance at 70 kg 0.134 against 0.135 L/h, volume 8.05 against 7.97 L, absorption rate 1.09 against 1.07 per hour, lag 0.88 against 0.89 h. The PD quantities move as little: baseline activity 99.1 against 99.0 %, turnover time 18.3 h in both, EC50 1.12 mg/L in both, and the between-subject SDs of the log turnover time (0.129 against 0.116) and of log EC50 (0.46 against 0.45) within a few hundredths. What the joint model adds here is small because the PK posterior is tight: 253 concentrations pin each subject's clearance and volume, so fixing their medians loses little, and the PD data have little to say about the PK quantities. The visible changes are on the noise side: the joint model's PK noise scale is 0.37 against 0.34 mg/L and its between-subject SD of log volume 0.149 against 0.135, since the PD channel now also weighs on the latent PK values.

Each fit runs its chains through completion_warmup_mcmc, which returns once three of the four hold their draws; the chain still warming up is left out and named here. Divergent transitions are counted over the retained draws: two in the PK fit and one in the PD fit, 64 of 3000 draws (2.1 %) in the joint model, whose 242 parameters couple each subject's seven latent quantities through the ODE. Every R-hat in the tables above is at most 1.014 and every bulk ESS at least 246 (the lag's between-subject SD, whose posterior reaches down to zero). The seconds are wall-clock on four threads of the machine that ran the fit. The fits are not part of the docs build: each ran once, into its own directory under research/warfarin/results/, and the page reads the committed tables. The receipts say what they are the numbers of.

Provenance ​

Weber's StanCon 2018 contribution, Solving ODEs in the wild: Scalable pharmacometrics with Stan, holds the data, the two Stan programs (PK, PD) and the R scripts. The two-stage models here follow those programs statement by statement, on the data as his munge.R prepares them. His notebook prints no estimates, so the fits above have nothing published to be compared with; they are BRM's own. The joint model is not part of his example.

Reproduce ​

From the repository root, with the test environment bootstrapped (julia --project=test test/setup_env.jl):

sh
julia -t 4 --startup-file=no --project=test research/warfarin/fit.jl

It writes one directory of tables per fit under research/warfarin/results/. The figures are AlgebraOfVega specifications in research/warfarin/figures.jl, drawn from those tables when the docs are built; julia --project=research/adaptive_centering/plots research/warfarin/figures.jl writes PNG previews of them to a scratch directory. The lowering and stanc checks of the three declarations run without a fit:

sh
BRM_WARFARIN_RUNTIME=0 julia --startup-file=no --project=test research/warfarin/reproduce.jl
BRM_WARFARIN_JOINT_RUNTIME=0 julia --startup-file=no --project=test research/warfarin/joint_reproduce.jl
